title: The Ocean's Climate Service Is Under Pressure
title_zh: 海洋的“气候服务”正承受压力
source_name: UN News / Ocean's ability to absorb carbon is weakening as climate change intensifies, UN warns
summary_zh: 联合国 10 月 28 日发布《2026 年气候技术进展报告》：海洋吸收了人类排放的约 30% 的二氧化碳和约 90% 的多余热量，但气候变化已使海洋吸收碳的能力下降约 6%。报告指出，南大洋、印度洋、北极等海域缺乏可靠的监测数据，呼吁加强“海洋碳情报”；并比较了三类海洋气候技术：海洋监测、红树林和海草等“蓝碳”生态系统，以及仍不成熟的海洋二氧化碳移除技术。作者提醒，这些技术不能代替减排。本文适合积累雅思环境类话题的词汇和数据表达。
paragraphs: For thousands of years, the ocean has quietly helped to keep our planet stable. It absorbs around 30 per cent of the carbon dioxide that humans release and about 90 per cent of the extra heat trapped by greenhouse gases. Without this natural service, global warming would be far more severe than it is today.

However, a new United Nations report, released on 28 October ahead of the COP31 climate conference in November, warns that this service is weakening. According to the report, climate change has already reduced the ocean's capacity to absorb carbon by approximately six per cent. Rising temperatures, acidification, pollution and damaged ecosystems are all disrupting the processes that allow the sea to store carbon. As a result, more carbon dioxide stays in the atmosphere, which in turn causes further warming.

"For a long time the ocean has been doing us an enormous climate service, but that service is under increasing pressure," said Sara Traerup, the lead author of the report. She also warned that the decline could speed up in the near future.

One major problem is that scientists simply do not have enough information. Reliable monitoring data is especially scarce in the Southern and Indian Oceans, the Arctic and many coastal areas. For this reason, the report calls for stronger "ocean carbon intelligence", which means combining science, technology, data and local knowledge to understand how the ocean handles carbon. As Traerup put it, "what we don't know, we cannot manage and protect."

The report examines three types of ocean climate technology. The first is ocean monitoring, such as sensors, observation systems and computer models, which is the most mature and the most urgently needed. The second is "blue carbon" ecosystems, including mangroves, seagrasses and salt marshes. These habitats already capture around 407 million tonnes of carbon dioxide every year, and they also protect coastlines and support local livelihoods. The third is marine carbon dioxide removal, which tries to take carbon out of the air and lock it away for a long time. Although it may be promising, it remains highly uncertain and needs much more research and regulation.
Most importantly, the authors stress that the ocean is not a shortcut. Ocean-based technologies should complement, rather than replace, cutting emissions and protecting nature on land and at sea.
paragraphs_zh: 数千年来，海洋一直默默地帮助地球保持稳定。人类排放的二氧化碳中约有 30% 被它吸收，温室气体困住的多余热量中约有 90% 也被它吸收。如果没有这种天然的“服务”，全球变暖会比现在严重得多。
然而，联合国在 11 月 COP31 气候大会召开之前，于 10 月 28 日发布的一份新报告警告说，海洋的这种“服务”正在减弱。报告称，气候变化已经使海洋吸收碳的能力下降了约 6%。气温上升、海水酸化、污染以及生态系统受损，都在扰乱海洋储存碳的过程。结果，更多的二氧化碳留在大气中，进而导致进一步变暖。
报告主要作者萨拉·特鲁普说：“长期以来，海洋一直在为我们提供巨大的气候服务，但这种服务正承受着越来越大的压力。”她还警告说，这种下降在不久的将来可能会加速。
一个主要问题是，科学家掌握的信息根本不够。在南大洋、印度洋、北极以及许多沿海地区，可靠的监测数据尤其匮乏。因此，报告呼吁加强“海洋碳情报”，也就是把科学、技术、数据和当地知识结合起来，弄清海洋是如何处理碳的。正如特鲁普所说：“我们不了解的东西，就无法管理和保护。”
报告考察了三类海洋气候技术。第一类是海洋监测，例如传感器、观测系统和计算机模型，这是最成熟、也最迫切需要的技术。第二类是“蓝碳”生态系统，包括红树林、海草床和盐沼。这些栖息地每年已经吸收约 4.07 亿吨二氧化碳，同时还能保护海岸线、维持当地人的生计。第三类是海洋二氧化碳移除技术，它试图把碳从空气中取出并长期封存起来。这种技术虽然可能前景不错，但仍有很大的不确定性，还需要更多的研究和监管。
最重要的是，作者们强调，海洋不是一条捷径。基于海洋的技术应当作为减排以及保护陆地和海洋自然环境的补充，而不是替代。
